entries.title: Effect of Cooling Time on Demoulding Temperature, Shrinkage and Warpage of Injection-Moulded Polypropylene Parts
entries.machine: injection-moulding research cell at RWTH Aachen IKV; exact press model not used in this registry pass
entries.tool: housing-part injection mould used for controlled cooling-time and thermal-condition experiments
entries.scale: PCR 3^3 full-factorial experiment plus a nine-level virgin-PP cooling-time experiment; exact replicate/cycle count is not used as a corpus total

raw.license: article open access; reusable raw experimental rows not confirmed public

entries.limitation: The measured cooling-time and demoulding-temperature relationships are specific to the housing geometry, PP feedstocks, thermal boundary conditions and tested mould. No cooling duration, demoulding temperature, shrinkage or warpage value is a universal production target.

entries.title: Optimisation of the Injection Moulding Process for Thick-Walled Parts Using Conformal Cooling Channels and CuBe Alloy Inserts
entries.journal: International Journal of Precision Engineering and Manufacturing
entries.machine: injection-moulding experimental cell used for three manufactured mould configurations; exact press model not used in registry
entries.material: PP-R engineering thermoplastic used for thick-walled component experiments.
entries.tool: manufactured conventional 316L mould, 316L conformal-cooling mould and CuBe cavity mould
entries.scale: three physically manufactured mould configurations with monitored injection trials and physical part testing

raw.license: article CC BY 4.0; reusable raw process traces not confirmed public

entries.limitation: Cooling performance and mechanical response depend on the thick-wall geometry, PP-R grade, channel design, coolant system and mould materials. Reported cycle-time, temperature and strength changes must not be promoted as universal conformal-cooling or CuBe rules.

entries.title: Influence of injection moulding parameters on the molecular weight distribution and mechanical behaviour of polypropylene
entries.machine: controlled injection-moulding experimental system; exact press model not extracted in this registry pass
entries.tool: controlled injection-moulding specimen tooling for processing-structure-property experiments
entries.scale: factorial experiments across three melt temperatures and two injection pressures with physical, thermal, rheological and mechanical characterization

raw.license: open-access article; publisher states data available on request

entries.limitation: The processing-structure-property relationship is bounded to the studied polypropylene, specimen geometry and thermal/shear history. The tested melt temperatures and pressures are experimental factors, not universal PP degradation limits or production settings.

entries.title: Optimization of injection molding parameters for automotive brake fluid reservoirs: design of experiments study across 27 industrial machines
entries.machine: 27 industrial presses: 14 Yizumi and 13 Haitian machines spanning approximately 150-400 tonnage classes.
entries.material: Ten polypropylene grades used across automotive brake-fluid-reservoir production.
entries.tool: 50 automotive reservoir product variants manufactured under industrial production conditions
entries.scale: 1,320 physical experiments across 27 industrial machines, 10 PP grades and 50 product variants

raw.license: CC BY 4.0 article; raw data stated available from authors

entries.limitation: Despite its unusually broad industrial scale, the study is one reservoir product family and an imbalanced machine/material experiment. Its fitted numerical optimum, machine-material pairings and specification values must not be generalized to unrelated moulds, materials or production sites.

entries.title: A State-Aware Hybrid Modeling Framework for Energy Prediction in Injection Molding
entries.journal: International Journal of Precision Engineering and Manufacturing-Green Technology
entries.machine: multiple injection-moulding equipment configurations used in the experimental campaign; exact machines remain study-specific
entries.material: PLA, PBS, virgin PP, recycled PP and modified recycled PP.
entries.tool: injection-moulding experiments spanning multiple materials, process conditions and equipment configurations
outcomes: measured energy required per injection-moulded part
entries.scale: comprehensive multi-material experimental injection-moulding dataset partitioned for model development and held-out testing; exact observation count not used in registry

raw.license: article CC BY 4.0; reusable raw experimental dataset not confirmed in this registry pass

entries.limitation: The study validates energy-prediction behavior for its five material systems and tested equipment/process states. Model accuracy and energy relationships are not physical root-cause proof and do not establish universal energy baselines, process settings or material rankings.
